arxiv-2103-12397.title: The topological counterparts of non-Hermitian SSH models
arxiv-2103-12397.creator: Y. Z. Han, J. S. Liu, C. S. Liu
arxiv-2103-12397.description: Abstract The breakdown of the conventional bulk-boundary correspondence due to non-Hermitian skin effect leads to the non-Bloch bulk-boundary correspondence in the generalized Brillouin zone. Inspired by the case of the equivalence between the non-reciprocal hopping and imaginary gauge field, we propose a method to construct the topological equivalent models of the non-Hermitian dimerized lattices with the similarity transformations.

arxiv-2103-15103.title: Phism: Polyhedral High-Level Synthesis in MLIR Conference: 1st Workshop on Languages, Tools, and Techniques for Accelerator Design; April 15, 2021; Virtual, Earth
arxiv-2103-15103.creator: Ruizhe Zhao, Jianyi Cheng
arxiv-2103-15103.description: Abstract . Polyhedral optimisation, a methodology that views nested loops as polyhedra and searches for their optimal transformation regarding specific objectives (parallelism, locality, etc.), sounds promising for mitigating difficulties in automatically optimising hardware designs described by high-level synthesis (HLS), which are typically software programs with nested loops.

arxiv-2110-05058.title: Observation of Exchange Bias in Antiferromagnetic Cr 0.79 Se due to Coexistence of Itinerant Weak Ferromagnetism at Low-temperature
arxiv-2110-05058.creator: Sayan Routh, Setti Thirupathaiah
arxiv-2110-05058.description: Abstract We report on the structural, electrical transport, and magnetic properties of antiferromagnetic transition-metal monochalcogenide Cr 0.79 Se. Different from the existing off-stoichiometric compositions, Cr 0.79 Se is found to be synthesised into the same NiAs-type hexagonal crystal structure of CrSe. Resistivity data suggest Cr 0.

arxiv-2112-14263.title: Multi-Field Q-balls with Real Scalars
arxiv-2112-14263.creator: Olivier Lennon
arxiv-2112-14263.description: Abstract Multi-field Q-balls, in which some, but not all, of the constituent fields are real scalars, are studied. Uncharged fields may classically contribute to Q-balls provided that their effect is to not destabilise the resulting object. The thin-wall limit is reviewed based on existing literature. Sufficient conditions for the theories that can plausibly contain thick-wall solutions are derived.

arxiv-2305-15194.title: DiffBlender: Scalable and Composable Multimodal Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
arxiv-2305-15194.creator: Sungnyun Kim, Junsoo Lee, Kibeom Hong, Daesik Kim, Namhyuk Ahn
arxiv-2305-15194.description: Abstract In this study, we aim to extend the capabilities of diffusion-based text-to-image (T2I) generation models by incorporating diverse modalities beyond textual description, such as sketch, box, color palette, and style embedding, within a single model. We thus design a multimodal T2I diffusion model, coined as DiffBlender , by separating the channels of conditions into three types, i.e.

arxiv-2306-10305.title: Suspended dry pick-up and flip-over assembly for van der Waals heterostructures with ultra-clean surfaces
arxiv-2306-10305.description: Abstract Van der Waals heterostructures are an excellent platform for studying intriguing interface phenomena, such as moiré and proximity effects. Surface science techniques like scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) have proven a powerful tool to study such heterostructures but have so far been hampered because of their high sensitivity to surface contamination.

arxiv-2407-03523.title: Inferring IGM parameters from the redshifted 21-cm Power Spectrum using Artificial Neural Networks
arxiv-2407-03523.creator: Sambit K. Giri
arxiv-2407-03523.description: Abstract The high redshift 21-cm signal promises to be a crucial probe of the state of the intergalactic medium (IGM). Understanding the connection between the observed 21-cm power spectrum and the physical quantities intricately associated with the IGM is crucial to fully understand the evolution of our Universe.

arxiv-2506-05459.title: RUBIES: A Spectroscopic Census of Little Red Dots
arxiv-2506-05459.creator: Raphael E. Hviding, Anna de Graaff, Tim B. Miller, David J. Setton, Jenny E. Greene, Ivo Labbé, Gabriel Brammer, Rachel Bezanson, Leindert A. Boogaard, Nikko J. Cleri, Joel Leja, Michael V. Maseda, Ian McConachie, Jorryt Matthee, Rohan P. Naidu, Pascal A. Oesch, Bingjie Wang (王冰洁), Katherine E. Whit
arxiv-2506-05459.description: Abstract The physical nature of Little Red Dots (LRDs) – a population of compact, red galaxies revealed by JWST – remains unclear. Photometric samples are constructed from varying selection criteria with limited spectroscopic follow-up available to test intrinsic spectral shapes and prevalence of broad emission lines.

arxiv-2508-20795.title: Time Series Embedding and Combination of Forecasts: A Reinforcement Learning Approach
arxiv-2508-20795.creator: Marcelo C. Medeiros, Jeronymo M. Pinto
arxiv-2508-20795.description: Abstract The forecasting combination puzzle is a well-known phenomenon in forecasting literature, stressing the challenge of outperforming the simple average when aggregating forecasts from diverse methods. This study proposes a Reinforcement Learning - based framework as a dynamic model selection approach to address this puzzle. Our framework is evaluated through extensive forecasting exercises using simulated and real data.

pmc-11360075.title: Design and Optimization of 3D-Printed Tablets Containing Mucuna Extracts for Erectile Dysfunction Management: A DoE-Guided Study
pmc-11360075.creator: Ratchapoom Wattanawiggan, Sunee Chansakaow, Pensak Jantrawut, Pattaraporn Panraksa, Jutamas Jiaranaikulwanitch, Suruk Udomsom, Patnarin Worajittiphon, Pratchaya Tipduangta

Mucuna, or M. pruriens, contains levodopa, a compound showing promise in ED treatment. However, formulating Mucuna extract into tablet dosage forms is challenging due to its semisolid nature.

pmc-11446993.title: Epidemiologic and clinical features of multisystem atrophy: a population-based study in Navarre, Spain
pmc-11446993.creator: M. E. Erro, P. Arrondo, I. Gastón, P. Clavero, J. Sánchez Ruiz de Gordoa, G. Martí Andrés, R. Valentí, J. Delfrade, E. Vicente
pmc-11446993.description: BackgroundEpidemiological studies on multisystem atrophy (MSA) are scarce. Our aim has been to analyse 10-year incidence, point prevalence, survival, and the time to diagnosis of MSA in Navarre, a northern Spanish region.MethodsThis is a population-based observational retrospective study, from 2012 to 2021, which covered the population of Navarre (followed until 31 December 2021).

pmc-11513585.title: Multiple mechanisms enable broad-spectrum activity of the Pelargonium sidoides root extract EPs 7630 against acute respiratory tract infections
pmc-11513585.creator: Jindrich Cinatl, Mark N. Wass, Martin Michaelis
pmc-11513585.description: There is clinical evidence showing that the Pelargonium sidoides root extract EPs 7630 is a safe and effective treatment for a range of acute infectious respiratory illnesses. Moreover, EPs 7630 has been shown to reduce the use of antibiotics, which is important in the context of rising antibiotic resistance levels.

pmc-12372066.title: Effects of Glycerol and Phenolics on Myceliophthora heterothallica Endoxylanase Expressed in K. phaffii
pmc-12372066.creator: Jéssica de Araujo Zanoni, Izabela Karolina Costa Zilli, Guilherme de Paula Pretto, Flavio Augusto Vicente Seixas, Marcela Marques de Freitas Lima, Eliana Gertrudes de Macedo Lemos, Eleni Gomes, Gabriel Zazeri, Gustavo Orlando Bonilla-Rodriguez, Gerald Lushington
pmc-12372066.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Industrial applications of xylanases in high-temperature settings are limited by enzyme instability. This study evaluated glycerol and phenolic compounds as modulators of the catalytic and structural properties of a recombinant Myceliophthora heterothallica endoxylanase (rMhXyn) expressed in Komagataella phaffii. Glycerol (20% v/v) significantly improved thermostability (5-fold increase in half-life at 55 °C), decreased the activation energy for catalysis, and enhanced structural rigidity as evidenced by molecular dynamics simulations (reduced RMSD and Rg).

pmc-12387831.title: Comparing Non-Invasive and Fluorescein Tear Break-Up Time in a Pre-Operative Refractive Surgery Population: Implications for Clinical Diagnosis
pmc-12387831.creator: Rebecca Cairns, Richard N McNeely, Mark C M Dunne, Raquel Gil-Cazorla, Shehzad A Naroo, Jonathan E Moore, Kyung Chul Yoon
pmc-12387831.description: Objectives: Fluorescein break-up time (FBUT) is commonly used to assess tear film stability. However, the instillation of fluorescein destabilises the tear film, impacting validity and clinical applicability, while the subjective nature and variation in volume and concentration reduces repeatability. Non-invasive break-up time (NIBUT) offers an alternative method with less potential bias.

pmc-12461324.title: Adsorption Studies of Fibrin Proteins onto Au- and Ag-Nanoparticles
pmc-12461324.creator: Walter Makgoba, Abram Mahladisa, Malili Matshaba, Mulatedzi Gandamipfa, Nikiwe Mhlanga, Teboho Mokhena, Lucky Sikhwivhilu, Thuto Mosuang
pmc-12461324.description: Au- and Ag-nanoparticles were synthesized and conjugated with fibrin protein samples through a sodium citrate-induced method for possible ‘AuNPs+fibrin’ and ‘AgNPs+fibrin’ corona formation adsorption studies. Average spherical diameter sizes of 11, 18, 45, and 50 nm of Au-nanoparticles and 12, 14, and 26 nm of Ag-nanoparticles were considered for the conjugation process.

pmc-13050769.title: Research progress on nucleic acid amplification–based detection technologies for phytopathogenic fungi
pmc-13050769.creator: Baoyu Wang, Mei Liu, Hui Wang, Chenfang Wang, Wei Zhang, Jiye Yan
pmc-13050769.description: AbstractPhytopathogenic fungi are highly diverse and globally distributed, posing a major threat to agricultural production worldwide. The annual losses caused by plant diseases can reach up to 30% of global crop yields, with over 80% of infections caused by fungal pathogens. The accurate identification of pathogenic fungal species is crucial for effective disease prevention and control.

pmc-13236639.title: Comparative maternal-fetal outcomes associated with different antihypertensive treatment strategies in preeclampsia: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-13236639.creator: Lin Zhao, Rui Chen, Yahui Xu, Haiying Wu
pmc-13236639.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundPreeclampsia seriously threatens maternal and infant health. Antihypertensive therapy is key to improving perinatal outcomes, yet comparative maternal-fetal evidence for oral agents remains limited.ObjectiveTo compare maternal–fetal outcomes of oral labetalol versus oral nifedipine in preeclampsia, informing individualized clinical treatment.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included consecutive preeclampsia patients admitted from January 2023 to December 2025, divided into Labetalol (n = 154) and nifedipine (n = 136) groups.
